‘The greatness of a nation and its moral progress can be judged by the way its animals are treated.’ — Mahatma Gandhi 

Equilibrium (2002) is a dystopian sci fi action film set in Libria, a future society where emotions are completely banned. To keep everyone numb and obedient, citizens are forced to take a drug called Prozium that suppresses all feelings.

Christian Bale plays John Preston, an elite enforcer trained to hunt down anyone who dares to feel and destroy things like art, music, and books. But everything changes when he misses a dose and starts experiencing emotions for the first time.

As he begins to feel both the beauty and pain his world has erased, Preston quietly turns against the system. He connects with an underground resistance and ends up using his own skills against the government he once blindly served.

source_details.title: Equilibrium
source_details.synopsis: Equilibrium is a 2002 American science fiction dystopian action film written and directed by Kurt Wimmer, and starring Christian Bale, Emily Watson, and Taye Diggs. The film follows Bale as John Preston, an enforcement officer in a future in which feelings and artistic expression are outlawed, and a society where its citizens are forced to take psychoactive drugs to suppress emotion. After accidentally missing a dose, Preston awakens and begins to uncover the suspicious inner workings of the regime governing the totalitarian state.
